marble.name: Multiplying fractions
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Understand a/b as a multiple of 1/b; multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by visual models (e.g. 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5)
marble.prompt: If a recipe uses 2/3 of a cup of butter and you wants to make it three times over, can they work out how much butter they need in total?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Multiplies the denominator too: 4 × 3/8 = 12/32, applying the whole number to both parts instead of just the count of unit fractions.
Incompletely distributes over a mixed number: 2 1/3 × 3 = 6 1/3, multiplying the whole but forgetting the fraction part.
Confuses the operation with addition (adds 4 + 3/8) or cannot see 5 × 1/4 as five quarters.
representations: Number line with repeated equal jumps of the unit/non-unit fraction
Fraction bars showing n copies of a/b combined
Repeated-addition equation aligned with the (n×a)/b rule

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Writes 12/32 (or reduces it back to 3/8); the denominator changes when it shouldn't.
wrongAnswers.fix: Return to repeated addition on a number line: 4 × 3/8 is four hops of three-eighths; the eighth (the unit) never changes, only how many. Contrast 12/32 = 3/8 — the answer didn't grow, so it can't be four lots.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Answer keeps the original fraction part (6 1/3) instead of tripling it; only the 2 was multiplied.
wrongAnswers.fix: Show three whole 2 1/3 bars: three 2s AND three thirds; or convert to 7/3 first and multiply. Emphasise every part is copied three times.

before.name: Fractions as sums of unit fractions
before.reason: a/b as sum of 1/b is prerequisite to understanding a/b as multiple of 1/b
